text:
Maya: quick scrub before I sign off, leaving primary coverage to Sam for the next 8h, Erin is secondary. I'm handing over the incident context below.

Maya: summary — yesterday evening we had a 30m embedding-autoscaler thrash during peak that caused token-p95 for embedding requests to jump to ~900ms for affected nodes. Not a full outage but customer throughput degraded for a small subset of requests.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: #INC-2345 — embeddings-autoscaler-high-p95 (severity: sev2) — 3776539200

Maya: Impact: 3 paying customers (org ids masked), intermittent request 429s during the thrash window; no data loss. Billing/usage unaffected.

Sam: got it. what's the current state?

Erin: last check 20m ago it looked stable; autoscaler scaled down and KV cache warmed. Logs showed OOM evictions on one node but pod restarted and rejoined.

Liu: i left a short note in the runbook about the temporary fix — we applied a conservative scaling cap to avoid overscaling noisy traffic.

Maya: runbook (internal): https://internal.redwood/runbooks/embeddings-autoscaler-troubleshooting — follow the "temporary throttle and cap" section if it recurs.

Maya: quick commands we ran:
```
# inspect autoscaler events
kubectl -n inference get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=autoscaler-processor-xyz
# diagnose memory usage
kubectl top pod autoscaler-processor-xyz -n inference
```

Sam: confirmed I can access dashboards. I'll keep a closer eye on p95 and the horizontal pod autoscaler (HPA) metrics for the next 2h. Will escalate if p95 > 600ms for >5m. :eyes:

Erin: I'll be on standby for infra rollback if the cap causes throttling elsewhere. pls ping me directly if you see increased 429s.

Maya: next steps before I go: 1) Follow-up ticket created for postmortem and capacity tuning: ENG-5123. 2) Add longer-term fix proposal to backlog (quantify memory pressure patterns). 3) Notify account execs for the 3 affected customers — CS already has a blurb.

ops-bot: PagerDuty note attached to #INC-2345: "Severity lowered to monitoring" — 3776541200

Sam: action items for me: 1) monitor p95 and HPA for 2h, 2) run the memory-snapshot command every 30m for first hour, 3) escalate to platform if recurring.

Sam: memory-snapshot command (quick):
```
kubectl exec -n inference -it autoscaler-processor-xyz -- bash -lc "pmap -x 1 | sort -k3 -nr | head"
```

Erin: coverage note — APAC night window has no dedicated primary, still need volunteer for local-night watch next week. Maya, can you flag in rotation?

Maya: noted. I'm opening a rotation-gap ticket to recruit 1 volunteer from APAC-eng by EOD: ORG-APAC-COVER.

Liu: I'll follow up on tuning proposals and postmortem draft tomorrow morning.

Sam: copying the quick monitoring checklist I'll run: p95 > 600ms -> open immediate page; sustained >5m -> flip autoscaler cap; any 503/429 spike -> notify CS and activate customer mitigation playbook.

Maya: thanks — leaving detailed notes in the incident thread and the runbook link above. Signing off now. Good luck and ping if anything. :thumbsup:

Sam: thanks Maya — will take it from here.

Erin: cheers, have a good one.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: #INC-2345 status changed to RESOLVED -> monitoring at 3776543600 (note: monitoring window until 3776547200)

Sam: noted the monitoring window. I'll keep an eye until at least 3776544410 then hand back to oncall rotation.

Maya: (reacts :white_check_mark:)
